findings.title: Go pipeline contrast does not isolate initialization-induced local minima
findings.source_claim: Controlled experiments isolate whether RL training from scratch is the major factor and rigorously evaluate whether passive pretraining impairs escape from local minima.
findings.suspect_step: Inferring an isolated initialization/local-minimum mechanism from a contrast that also changes the KL-anchored training objective.
findings.check: Source p6 explicitly adds KL to SPT-then-RFT and Figure2 varies its coefficient. The contrast identifies combined pipeline behavior. Existing strictly concave KL illustration shows the same direction of reward gap can occur at a unique global optimum, so the contrast alone does not identify optimization trapping.
assumptions: Use only the documented RPT versus SPT-then-RFT designs and their explicit KL distinction.
Do not assume measured Go scores are false or actual local minima absent.
The cached one-state bandit is an identification illustration, not an instance of the Go experimental environment.
No matched-objective isolation control is reported in the checked Section4.1/AppendixB.1.
counterevidence: KL penalty is openly introduced to mimic realistic LLM finetuning, and its coefficient dependence is reported.
Source p6 states no-KL/infinite-budget convergence to the same optimum.
These qualifications support the complete-pipeline comparison and preserve the reported66%/92% outcomes, but do not establish the stronger isolation claimed on p5.
All LLM experimental conditions begin from pretrained Qwen; source explicitly calls it a finetuning proxy.
findings.dependency: The claimed mechanism is a central empirical justification in Section4.1 for replacing passive pretraining. Invalidating this inferential step materially damages that specific justification; the broad recommendation and descriptive win rates can survive.

repair.statement: Restrict the conclusion to the evaluated complete pipelines; alternatively separate initialization from the KL objective and supply evidence identifying optimization trapping before retaining the isolated mechanism claim.
repair.verification: Scope restriction is supported. Matched-objective comparison, actual mechanism and corrected empirical results have not been verified.

findings.remaining_question: Did the actual Go optimization path encounter initialization-induced trapping, and how much of the gap is due to the anchored objective?

open_items.question: Was the displayed mixed-language prompt actually used?
What weighting/repetition yields29%, and what denominator yields0.02 for one Fibonacci example?
What exact verification and manual output-correction rules underlie orthogonality scores?

scope_clarifications: Language-model comparison is explicitly a finetuning proxy
No proof of RPT necessity claimed verified
Proposed short-context architecture not an executed result
supported_impact: F02 establishes invalid isolation of a core empirical mechanism; F01 remains a Minor published-protocol inconsistency. Descriptive scores and the broader proposal are not refuted.
